79	    def __init__(self, store: LedgerStore, initial_balance: int = DEFAULT_INITIAL_BALANCE) -> None:
80	        self.store = store
81	        self.initial_balance = initial_balance
82	        # Record the endowment convention so persisted fork replay checks and
83	        # recovery use the same value the service was configured with.

89	    def submit_transaction(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
90	        """Validate and enqueue a transaction. Returns (status, body)."""
91	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
92	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
93	        for field in REQUIRED_TX_FIELDS:
94	            if field not in payload:
95	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
96	
97	        sender = payload["from"]
98	        recipient = payload["to"]
99	        amount = payload["amount"]
100	        signature = payload["signature"]
101	
102	        if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
103	            return 400, {"error": "field 'from' must be a non-empty string"}
104	        if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
105	            return 400, {"error": "field 'to' must be a non-empty string"}
106	        # bool is a subclass of int: reject it and all non-int types explicitly.
107	        if not isinstance(amount, int) or isinstance(amount, bool) or amount <= 0:
108	            return 400, {"error": "field 'amount' must be a positive integer"}
109	        if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
110	            return 400, {"error": "field 'signature' must be a non-empty string"}
111	
112	        message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
113	        if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
114	            return 400, {"error": "invalid signature"}
115	
116	        tx = Transaction(sender, recipient, amount, signature)
117	        with self.store.lock:
118	            if tx.tx_id in self.store.pending:
119	                return 409, {"error": "transaction already pending", "tx_id": tx.tx_id}
120	            if any(tx.tx_id == existing.tx_id for block in self.store.chain for existing in block.transactions):
121	                return 409, {"error": "transaction already confirmed", "tx_id": tx.tx_id}
122	            if self.available_balance(sender) < amount:
123	                return 400, {"error": "insufficient balance"}
124	            self.store.pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
125	            try:
126	                self.store.save()
127	            except BaseException:
128	                # Persistence failed: drop the in-memory enqueue so memory
129	                # keeps matching the last durably committed state.
130	                self.store.pending.pop(tx.tx_id, None)
131	                raise
132	        return 202, {"tx_id": tx.tx_id}

136	    def mine_block(self) -> tuple[int, dict]:
137	        """Pack all pending transactions (ascending tx_id) into a pending block.
138	
139	        Only allowed when the chain tip is confirmed; the new block becomes
140	        the pending tip until it is confirmed or rolled back.
141	        """
142	        with self.store.lock:
143	            if self.store.tip_is_pending():
144	                return 409, {"error": "tip block is pending confirmation"}
145	            if not self.store.pending:
146	                return 409, {"error": "no pending transactions"}
147	            ordered = sorted(self.store.pending.values(), key=lambda tx: tx.tx_id)
148	            block = Block.create(
149	                height=self.store.next_height(),
150	                prev_hash=self.store.tip_hash(),
151	                transactions=ordered,
152	                status=STATUS_PENDING,
153	            )
154	            self.store.chain.append(block)
155	            removed = [self.store.pending.pop(tx.tx_id) for tx in ordered]
156	            try:
157	                self.store.save()
158	            except BaseException:
159	                # Undo the in-memory block so nothing un-persisted is visible.
160	                self.store.chain.pop()
161	                self.store.pending.update({tx.tx_id: tx for tx in removed})
162	                raise
163	        return 201, {
164	            "height": block.height,
165	            "block_hash": block.block_hash,
166	            "merkle_root": block.merkle_root,
167	            "status": block.status,
168	        }

182	        height_int = _parse_height(height)

191	    def confirm_block(self, height: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
192	        """Confirm a pending tip block.
193	
194	        Only a pending chain tip whose parent is confirmed can be confirmed.
195	        Confirming an already-confirmed block is idempotent (200); every
196	        other case — unknown or malformed height, non-tip pending block —
197	        returns 409.
198	        """
199	        height_int = _parse_height(height)
200	        with self.store.lock:
201	            if height_int is None:
202	                return 409, {"error": "block cannot be confirmed"}
203	            block = self.store.block_at(height_int)
204	            if block is None:
205	                return 409, {"error": "block cannot be confirmed"}
206	            if block.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED:
207	                # Idempotent re-confirm.
208	                return 200, {"height": block.height, "status": STATUS_CONFIRMED}
209	            if block is not self.store.tip():
210	                return 409, {"error": "only the chain tip can be confirmed"}
211	            parent = self.store.chain[-2] if len(self.store.chain) >= 2 else None
212	            if parent is None or parent.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
213	                return 409, {"error": "previous block is not confirmed"}
214	            block.status = STATUS_CONFIRMED
215	            try:
216	                self.store.save()
217	            except BaseException:
218	                block.status = STATUS_PENDING
219	                raise
220	            return 200, {"height": block.height, "status": STATUS_CONFIRMED}

222	    def rollback_block(self, height: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
223	        """Roll back a pending tip block: delete it and restore its transactions.
224	
225	        Unknown or malformed heights (including an already-rolled-back
226	        height) return 404; a confirmed block or a non-tip block returns 409.
227	        """
228	        height_int = _parse_height(height)
229	        if height_int is None:
230	            return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
231	        with self.store.lock:
232	            block = self.store.block_at(height_int)
233	            if block is None:
234	                return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
235	            if block.status == STATUS_CONFIRMED:
236	                return 409, {"error": "confirmed block cannot be rolled back"}
237	            if block is not self.store.tip():
238	                return 409, {"error": "only the chain tip can be rolled back"}
239	            pending_before = set(self.store.pending)
240	            rolled_back = self.store.rollback_tip()
241	            try:
242	                self.store.save()
243	            except BaseException:
244	                # Restore the block and drop only the mempool entries we added.
245	                self.store.chain.append(rolled_back)
246	                for tx_id in list(self.store.pending):
247	                    if tx_id not in pending_before:
248	                        del self.store.pending[tx_id]
249	                raise
250	            return 200, {"height": rolled_back.height, "status": "rolled_back"}

252	    def get_proof(self, height: object, tx_id: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
253	        """Return a Merkle inclusion proof for tx_id at the given height.
254	
255	        Returns 404 for an unknown height, a malformed height/tx_id, or a
256	        transaction absent from that block. Proofs are only issued for
257	        confirmed blocks; a pending block returns 409.
258	        """
259	        height_int = _parse_height(height)
260	        if height_int is None:
261	            return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
262	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id):
263	            return 404, {"error": "transaction not found"}
264	        with self.store.lock:
265	            block = self.store.block_at(height_int)
266	            if block is None:
267	                return 404, {"error": "block not found"}
268	            if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
269	                return 409, {"error": "block is pending confirmation"}

271	            try:

275	            siblings = crypto.merkle_proof(tx_ids, index)
276	            return 200, {
277	                "height": block.height,
278	                "tx_id": tx_id,
279	                "index": index,
280	                "merkle_root": block.merkle_root,
281	                "block_hash": block.block_hash,
282	                "siblings": siblings,
283	            }

305	    def reported_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
306	        """Confirmed balance minus spends sitting in the pending tip block.
307	
308	        Pending-block credits are not counted: unconfirmed income can still
309	        be rolled back, so it must not inflate the reported balance.
310	        """
311	        balance = self.confirmed_balance(account)
312	        tip = self.store.tip()
313	        if tip.status == STATUS_PENDING:
314	            for tx in tip.transactions:
315	                if tx.sender == account:
316	                    balance -= tx.amount
317	        return balance

319	    def available_balance(self, account: str) -> int:
320	        """Reported balance minus amounts already committed in the mempool.
321	
322	        Pending credits (mempool or unconfirmed block) are deliberately not
323	        counted, so a sequence of submissions cannot spend money that has not
324	        been confirmed yet.
325	        """
326	        balance = self.reported_balance(account)
327	        for tx in self.store.pending.values():
328	            if tx.sender == account:
329	                balance -= tx.amount
330	        return balance

334	    @staticmethod
335	    def _fork_summary(blocks: list) -> dict:
336	        """Public fork descriptor S: tip_hash, height, length, status."""
337	        tip = blocks[-1]
338	        return {
339	            "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
340	            "height": tip.height,
341	            # The length counts every block including the genesis block.
342	            "length": len(blocks),
343	            "status": tip.status,
344	        }

346	    def _winning_fork(self) -> tuple[str, list]:
347	        """Pick the winner among the canonical chain and every candidate.
348	
349	        Longest chain wins; equal lengths are broken by the smallest tip hash
350	        (lexicographic hex order). Returns (tip_hash, block list).
351	        """
352	        contenders: list[tuple[str, list]] = [
353	            (self.store.tip_hash(), self.store.chain)
354	        ]
355	        contenders.extend(self.store.forks.items())
356	        contenders.sort(key=lambda item: (-len(item[1]), item[0]))
357	        return contenders[0]

359	    def submit_fork_candidate(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
360	        """POST /v1/forks/candidates — validate and store a candidate fork.
361	
362	        Returns 201 with the fork descriptor S. Malformed or invalid forks
363	        return 400; a fork already known (identical to the canonical tip or an
364	        existing candidate tip) returns 409.
365	        """
366	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
367	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
368	        blocks_raw = payload.get("blocks")
369	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
370	            return 400, {"error": "missing field: blocks (must be a list)"}
371	        try:
372	            fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
373	        except ValueError as exc:
374	            return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
375	        summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
376	        # An exported fork (the five-field {tip_hash, height, length, status,
377	        # blocks} document) may be resubmitted verbatim; every supplied summary
378	        # field is re-verified against the recomputed descriptor.
379	        for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
380	            if field in payload and payload[field] != summary[field]:
381	                return 400, {"error": f"summary field {field!r} does not match the blocks"}
382	        tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
383	        with self.store.lock:
384	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
385	            # A tip hash equal to any canonical block hash means the candidate
386	            # is exactly the canonical chain or a prefix of it (the block hash
387	            # binds height, parent and Merkle root), so it carries nothing new.
388	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
389	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
390	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
391	                return 409, {"error": "candidate fork already exists", "tip_hash": tip_hash}
392	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
393	            try:
394	                self.store.save()
395	            except BaseException:
396	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
397	                raise
398	        return 201, self._fork_summary(fork)

400	    def get_chain(self) -> tuple[int, dict]:
401	        """GET /v1/chain — canonical chain, candidates sorted by tip hash and
402	        the adoptable winner (a non-canonical chain that beats canonical).
403	        """
404	        with self.store.lock:
405	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
406	            canonical = self._fork_summary(self.store.chain)
407	            candidates = [
408	                self._fork_summary(self.store.forks[tip])
409	                for tip in sorted(self.store.forks)
410	            ]
411	            winner_tip, winner_chain = self._winning_fork()
412	            adoptable: list[dict] = []
413	            if winner_tip != self.store.tip_hash():
414	                adoptable.append(self._fork_summary(winner_chain))
415	            return 200, {
416	                "canonical": canonical,
417	                "candidates": candidates,
418	                "adoptable": adoptable,
419	            }

421	    def adopt_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
422	        """POST /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/adopt — atomically switch to the winner.
423	
424	        Unknown tips return 404; adopting anything other than the current
425	        winning (longest / smallest-tip-hash) chain returns 409. Adoption
426	        replaces the canonical chain and mempool in one atomic write that
427	        advances the generation and rebuilds all indexes; transactions unique
428	        to the old chain's confirmed history return to the mempool, while
429	        pending-block transactions never enter it.
430	        """
431	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
432	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
433	        with self.store.lock:
434	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
435	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
436	            if fork is None:
437	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
438	            winner_tip, _ = self._winning_fork()
439	            if winner_tip != tip_hash:
440	                return 409, {"error": "only the winning fork can be adopted"}
441	            old_chain = self.store.chain
442	            old_pending = dict(self.store.pending)
443	            self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash)
444	            self.store.replace_chain(fork)
445	            # An adopted synced tip keeps its sync records (queryable until
446	            # expiry); record the adoption once per provenance entry.
447	            adopted_keys = sorted(
448	                key
449	                for key, rec in self.store.syncs.items()
450	                if rec["tip_hash"] == tip_hash
451	            )
452	            for rec_source, request_id in adopted_keys:
453	                self.store.append_audit_event(
454	                    EVENT_SYNC_ADOPTED,
455	                    {
456	                        "source": rec_source,
457	                        "request_id": request_id,
458	                        "tip_hash": tip_hash,
459	                    },
460	                )
461	            try:
462	                self.store.save()
463	            except BaseException:
464	                # Restore the pre-adoption in-memory state on a failed write.
465	                self.store.chain = old_chain
466	                self.store.pending = old_pending
467	                self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
468	                self.store.rebuild_derived()
469	                del self.store.audit_events[len(self.store.audit_events) - len(adopted_keys) :]
470	                raise
471	            return 200, self._fork_summary(fork)

473	    def export_fork(self, tip_hash: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
474	        """GET /v1/forks/{tip_hash}/export — full export of a candidate fork.
475	
476	        Only stored candidates are exportable: the canonical tip, an unknown
477	        tip and a malformed tip hash (not 64 lowercase hex chars) all return
478	        404. The response carries exactly five fields — the fork descriptor
479	        (tip_hash, height, length, status, all describing the tip block) plus
480	        the full block list including the genesis block, every transaction's
481	        signature and an optional pending tip — and can be resubmitted to
482	        POST /v1/forks/candidates verbatim.
483	        """
484	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
485	            return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
486	        with self.store.lock:
487	            fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
488	            if fork is None:
489	                return 404, {"error": "unknown fork tip"}
490	            body = self._fork_summary(fork)
491	            body["blocks"] = [block.to_dict() for block in fork]
492	            return 200, body

499	    @staticmethod
500	    def _candidate_blocks(candidate: object) -> object:
501	        """Normalize a sync ``candidate`` to its raw blocks list.
502	
503	        The candidate follows the existing export format (the five-field
504	        ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, blocks}`` document); the
505	        ``{"blocks": [...]}`` wrapper and a bare block list are accepted too.
506	        """
507	        if isinstance(candidate, dict):
508	            return candidate.get("blocks")
509	        return candidate

511	    @staticmethod
512	    def _candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw: list) -> str:
513	        """Stable content fingerprint of a candidate's raw block list.
514	
515	        Used to decide whether a same-key retry carries the same candidate
516	        content. Key order and whitespace are normalized so two documents that
517	        serialize the same blocks identically compare equal.
518	        """
519	        return hashlib.sha256(
520	            json.dumps(blocks_raw, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False).encode("utf-8")
521	        ).hexdigest()

523	    def _prune_expired_syncs(self) -> list[str]:
524	        """Sweep expired sync records and persist the sweep atomically.
525	
526	        A candidate received through a sync lives only while its record is
527	        unexpired; on expiry both the record and its still-stored candidate fork
528	        are dropped, together and in a single atomic save that advances the
529	        generation. Candidates submitted directly (no sync record) never
530	        expire, and an adopted tip is no longer in ``forks`` (it is on the
531	        canonical chain), so its expiring audit record leaves the chain
532	        untouched. If the write fails the pre-cleanup records and forks are
533	        restored so no success is ever reported for an un-persisted sweep.
534	        Caller must hold the store lock. Returns the pruned tip hashes.
535	        """
536	        expired_tips, removed = self.store.prune_syncs()
537	        if not removed:
538	            return expired_tips
539	        removed_forks: dict[str, list] = {}
540	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain}
541	        # The same tip could theoretically be referenced by another live
542	        # record; only drop a fork nothing still points at.
543	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in self.store.syncs.values()}
544	        for tip in expired_tips:
545	            if tip in canonical_hashes or tip in live_tips:
546	                continue
547	            fork = self.store.forks.pop(tip, None)
548	            if fork is not None:
549	                removed_forks[tip] = fork
550	        # Record one permanent expiry event per removed sync record. A tip
551	        # already adopted onto the canonical chain still gets its event: the
552	        # record's expiry is auditable even though the chain is untouched.
553	        for (rec_source, request_id), rec in sorted(removed.items()):
554	            self.store.append_audit_event(
555	                EVENT_SYNC_EXPIRED,
556	                {
557	                    "source": rec_source,
558	                    "request_id": request_id,
559	                    "tip_hash": rec["tip_hash"],
560	                    "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
561	                },
562	            )
563	        try:
564	            self.store.save()
565	        except BaseException:
566	            # Restore the pre-cleanup state: a failed write must neither leave
567	            # the records gone nor their candidates orphaned, nor the events
568	            # durably visible.
569	            del self.store.audit_events[len(self.store.audit_events) - len(removed) :]
570	            self.store.restore_syncs(removed, removed_forks)
571	            raise
572	        return expired_tips

574	    def _tip_descriptor(self, tip_hash: str) -> dict | None:
575	        """Resolve (height/length/status) for a synced tip.
576	
577	        Looks the candidate up among stored forks first, then among canonical
578	        blocks, so audit rows remain available after the candidate is adopted.
579	        """
580	        fork = self.store.forks.get(tip_hash)
581	        if fork is not None:
582	            return self._fork_summary(fork)
583	        for block in self.store.chain:
584	            if block.block_hash == tip_hash:
585	                return {
586	                    "tip_hash": block.block_hash,
587	                    "height": block.height,
588	                    # Length counts every block including the genesis block.
589	                    "length": block.height + 1,
590	                    "status": block.status,
591	                }
592	        return None

594	    def submit_fork_sync(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
595	        """POST /v1/forks/sync — receive a candidate chain from another node.
596	
597	        The request carries ``source``, ``request_id``, ``expires_at`` (Unix
598	        seconds) and ``candidate`` (an export-format fork document).
599	
600	        Authorization. A *new* source+request_id pair is accepted only when the
601	        source is registered in the persistent trust registry with status
602	        ``active`` and an ``expires_at`` still in the future. An unknown,
603	        revoked or registry-expired source is rejected 403 before the candidate
604	        is examined. A retry on a still-live recorded key bypasses the registry
605	        check entirely: the recorded result must keep replaying even after the
606	        source has since been rotated, revoked or expired.
607	
608	        After authorization (and only then) the candidate is re-validated
609	        exactly like a direct candidate submission (canonical genesis,
610	        consecutive heights and prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and
611	        Merkle roots, tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique ascending tx_ids,
612	        endowment replay, pending-only-at-tip).
613	
614	        Status precedence: malformed envelope fields are 400; an unauthorized
615	        source is 403; a well-formed new request whose ``expires_at`` is not
616	        later than now is 410; a well-formed but failing candidate chain (or a
617	        tampered candidate summary) is 400. Returns 201 on first acceptance
618	        with ``{tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at}``. A retry with
619	        the same source + request_id and identical content replays the original
620	        result as 200; the same key with different content returns 409, as does
621	        a duplicate tip already known.
622	        """
623	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
624	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
625	        for field in ("source", "request_id", "expires_at", "candidate"):
626	            if field not in payload:
627	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
628	
629	        source = payload["source"]
630	        request_id = payload["request_id"]
631	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
632	        candidate = payload["candidate"]
633	
634	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
635	            return 400, {"error": "field 'source' must be a non-empty string"}
636	        if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
637	            return 400, {"error": "field 'request_id' must be a non-empty string"}
638	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
639	            return 400, {"error": "field 'expires_at' must be a Unix-seconds integer"}
640	
641	        blocks_raw = self._candidate_blocks(candidate)
642	        if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list):
643	            return 400, {"error": "field 'candidate' must contain a 'blocks' list"}
644	
645	        with self.store.lock:
646	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
647	
648	            key = (source, request_id)
649	            existing = self.store.syncs.get(key)
650	
651	            if existing is None:
652	                # Authorization gate for new deliveries only: the source must
653	                # be an active, unexpired entry of the persistent trust
654	                # registry. Unknown, revoked or registry-expired sources are
655	                # refused 403 before the candidate is examined. A retry on a
656	                # still-live key skips this, so a recorded result keeps
657	                # replaying even after the source has since been rotated,
658	                # revoked or expired.
659	                now = time.time()
660	                trusted = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
661	                if (
662	                    trusted is None
663	                    or trusted["status"] != TRUST_ACTIVE
664	                    or trusted["expires_at"] <= now
665	                ):
666	                    return 403, {"error": "source is not an active trusted source"}
667	                # The request's own deadline is checked next, still before the
668	                # candidate chain is examined: a well-formed request whose
669	                # expiry is not later than now is gone (410).
670	                if expires_at <= now:
671	                    return 410, {"error": "sync request has expired"}
672	
673	            # Re-validate the whole candidate chain and recompute the tip
674	            # summary BEFORE any idempotency decision: a request whose supplied
675	            # tip_hash/height/length/status were tampered with must fail 400,
676	            # never be answered with the cached 200 for its source+request_id.
677	            try:
678	                fork = self.store.validate_fork_blocks(blocks_raw)
679	            except ValueError as exc:
680	                return 400, {"error": str(exc)}
681	            summary = self._fork_summary(fork)
682	            if isinstance(candidate, dict):
683	                for field in ("tip_hash", "height", "length", "status"):
684	                    if field in candidate and candidate[field] != summary[field]:
685	                        return 400, {
686	                            "error": f"candidate field {field!r} does not match the blocks"
687	                        }
688	            tip_hash = fork[-1].block_hash
689	            fingerprint = self._candidate_fingerprint(blocks_raw)
690	
691	            if existing is not None:
692	                # A retry on a live key is idempotent only when it carries the
693	                # identical candidate content; a changed body conflicts 409.
694	                if fingerprint != existing["fingerprint"]:
695	                    return 409, {
696	                        "error": "request_id already used with different content"
697	                    }
698	                descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(existing["tip_hash"]) or {
699	                    "tip_hash": existing["tip_hash"],
700	                    "height": None,
701	                    "length": None,
702	                    "status": None,
703	                }
704	                return 200, {
705	                    "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
706	                    "height": descriptor.get("height"),
707	                    "length": descriptor.get("length"),
708	                    "status": descriptor.get("status"),
709	                    "expires_at": existing["expires_at"],
710	                }
711	
712	            if any(tip_hash == block.block_hash for block in self.store.chain):
713	                return 409, {"error": "fork is identical to the canonical chain"}
714	            if tip_hash in self.store.forks:
715	                return 409, {
716	                    "error": "candidate fork already exists",
717	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
718	                }
719	
720	            self.store.forks[tip_hash] = fork
721	            self.store.syncs[key] = {
722	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
723	                "expires_at": expires_at,
724	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
725	            }
726	            self.store.append_audit_event(
727	                EVENT_SYNC_RECEIVED,
728	                {
729	                    "source": source,
730	                    "request_id": request_id,
731	                    "tip_hash": tip_hash,
732	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
733	                },
734	            )
735	            try:
736	                self.store.save()
737	            except BaseException:
738	                # Roll back the candidate, its metadata and the audit event
739	                # together so a failed write never leaves one without the others.
740	                self.store.syncs.pop(key, None)
741	                self.store.forks.pop(tip_hash, None)
742	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
743	                raise
744	
745	            result = dict(summary)
746	            result["expires_at"] = expires_at
747	            return 201, result

749	    def list_fork_syncs(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
750	        """GET /v1/forks/sync — audit listing of received sync candidates.
751	
752	        Filters: ``source`` (exact), ``min_height`` and ``max_height``.
753	        ``limit`` defaults to 50 and must be 1-200; ``cursor`` defaults to 0.
754	        Every numeric value must be a plain decimal without leading zeros; a
755	        malformed value returns 400. Rows are ordered by
756	        ``(height, tip_hash, source)``; ``cursor == total`` returns an empty
757	        page, ``cursor > total`` returns 400. Each item carries
758	        ``source, request_id, tip_hash, height, length, status, expires_at``.
759	        """
760	        source = params.get("source")
761	        if source is not None and (not isinstance(source, str) or not source):
762	            return 400, {"error": "source must be a non-empty string"}
763	
764	        min_height = None
765	        if params.get("min_height") is not None:
766	            min_height = _parse_decimal(params["min_height"])
767	            if min_height is None:
768	                return 400, {"error": "min_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
769	        max_height = None
770	        if params.get("max_height") is not None:
771	            max_height = _parse_decimal(params["max_height"])
772	            if max_height is None:
773	                return 400, {"error": "max_height must be a non-negative decimal"}
774	        if min_height is not None and max_height is not None and min_height > max_height:
775	            return 400, {"error": "min_height must not exceed max_height"}
776	
777	        limit = self.SYNC_DEFAULT_LIMIT
778	        if params.get("limit") is not None:
779	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
780	            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.SYNC_MAX_LIMIT:
781	                return 400, {"error": "limit must be a decimal between 1 and 200"}
782	            limit = parsed
783	        cursor = 0
784	        if params.get("cursor") is not None:
785	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["cursor"])
786	            if parsed is None:
787	                return 400, {"error": "cursor must be a non-negative decimal"}
788	            cursor = parsed
789	
790	        with self.store.lock:
791	            self._prune_expired_syncs()
792	            rows: list[dict] = []
793	            for (rec_source, request_id), rec in self.store.syncs.items():
794	                if source is not None and rec_source != source:
795	                    continue
796	                descriptor = self._tip_descriptor(rec["tip_hash"])
797	                if descriptor is None:
798	                    continue
799	                if min_height is not None and descriptor["height"] < min_height:
800	                    continue
801	                if max_height is not None and descriptor["height"] > max_height:
802	                    continue
803	                rows.append(
804	                    {
805	                        "source": rec_source,
806	                        "request_id": request_id,
807	                        "tip_hash": descriptor["tip_hash"],
808	                        "height": descriptor["height"],
809	                        "length": descriptor["length"],
810	                        "status": descriptor["status"],
811	                        "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
812	                    }
813	                )
814	
815	        rows.sort(key=lambda row: (row["height"], row["tip_hash"], row["source"]))
816	        total = len(rows)
817	        if cursor > total:
818	            return 400, {"error": "cursor is beyond the result set"}
819	        items = rows[cursor : cursor + limit]
820	        next_cursor = cursor + limit if cursor + limit < total else None
821	        return 200, {"items": items, "total": total, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

829	    def list_transactions(self, params: dict) -> tuple[int, dict]:
830	        """GET /v1/index/transactions — paginated confirmed-chain tx index.
831	
832	        Pending-tip transactions are excluded. Filters (AND-combined):
833	        ``tx_id`` (64 lowercase hex), ``account`` (matches sender or
834	        recipient) and ``height``; ``limit`` (default 50, range 1-200) and
835	        ``cursor`` (default 0) paginate. Numeric filters must be plain
836	        decimals without leading zeros; any malformed value returns 400.
837	        Rows are ordered by (height, index, tx_id); ``index`` is the
838	        transaction's 0-based position inside its block, matching the Merkle
839	        proof index. A cursor beyond the filtered total returns 400, a cursor
840	        equal to it returns an empty page.
841	        """
842	        tx_id = params.get("tx_id")
843	        if tx_id is not None and not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id):
844	            return 400, {"error": "tx_id must be 64 lowercase hex characters"}
845	        account = params.get("account")
846	        if account is not None and (not isinstance(account, str) or not account):
847	            return 400, {"error": "account must be a non-empty string"}
848	
849	        height = None
850	        if params.get("height") is not None:
851	            height = _parse_decimal(params["height"])
852	            if height is None:
853	                return 400, {"error": "height must be a non-negative decimal"}
854	        limit = self.INDEX_DEFAULT_LIMIT
855	        if params.get("limit") is not None:
856	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["limit"])
857	            if parsed is None or not 1 <= parsed <= self.INDEX_MAX_LIMIT:
858	                return 400, {"error": "limit must be a decimal between 1 and 200"}
859	            limit = parsed
860	        cursor = 0
861	        if params.get("cursor") is not None:
862	            parsed = _parse_decimal(params["cursor"])
863	            if parsed is None:
864	                return 400, {"error": "cursor must be a non-negative decimal"}
865	            cursor = parsed
866	
867	        with self.store.lock:
868	            rows: list[dict] = []
869	            for block in self.store.chain:
870	                if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
871	                    continue
872	                if height is not None and block.height != height:
873	                    continue
874	                for index, tx in enumerate(block.transactions):
875	                    if tx_id is not None and tx.tx_id != tx_id:
876	                        continue
877	                    if account is not None and account not in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
878	                        continue
879	                    rows.append(
880	                        {
881	                            "tx_id": tx.tx_id,
882	                            "height": block.height,
883	                            "block_hash": block.block_hash,
884	                            "index": index,
885	                            "from": tx.sender,
886	                            "to": tx.recipient,
887	                            "amount": tx.amount,
888	                        }
889	                    )
890	        # Chain order is already (height, index) ascending; the tx_id
891	        # tiebreaker is implied because ids are unique within a block.
892	        total = len(rows)
893	        if cursor > total:
894	            return 400, {"error": "cursor is beyond the result set"}
895	        items = rows[cursor : cursor + limit]
896	        next_cursor = cursor + limit if cursor + limit < total else None
897	        return 200, {"items": items, "total": total, "next_cursor": next_cursor}

901	    @staticmethod
902	    def _trust_record(source: str, rec: dict) -> dict:
903	        """Public shape of one trust-source record."""
904	        return {
905	            "source": source,
906	            "public_key": rec["public_key"],
907	            "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
908	            "version": rec["version"],
909	            "status": rec["status"],
910	        }

912	    def _validate_trust_input(self, payload: object, require_version: bool) -> tuple | None:
913	        """Validate a trust registration/rotation body.
914	
915	        ``source`` must be a non-empty string, ``public_key`` 64 lowercase
916	        hex characters and ``expires_at`` a plain (non-boolean) integer.
917	        Rotation/revocation additionally require a positive integer
918	        ``expected_version``. Returns (source, public_key, expires_at[,
919	        expected_version]) or None after sending a 400.
920	        """
921	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
922	            return None
923	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
924	            if field not in payload:
925	                return None
926	        source = payload["source"]
927	        public_key = payload["public_key"]
928	        expires_at = payload["expires_at"]
929	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
930	            return None
931	        if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
932	            return None
933	        if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
934	            return None
935	        if not require_version:
936	            return source, public_key, expires_at
937	        expected_version = payload.get("expected_version")
938	        if (
939	            isinstance(expected_version, bool)
940	            or not isinstance(expected_version, int)
941	            or expected_version < 1
942	        ):
943	            return None
944	        return source, public_key, expires_at, expected_version

946	    def register_trust_source(self, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
947	        """POST /v1/trust/sources — register a trusted source.
948	
949	        A new source is created at version 1 with status ``active`` and the
950	        change is persisted together with its audit event in one atomic write
951	        (201). Re-posting the exact same (public_key, expires_at) content is
952	        idempotent (200, the stored record unchanged); the same source with
953	        different content conflicts (409).
954	        """
955	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
956	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
957	        for field in ("source", "public_key", "expires_at"):
958	            if field not in payload:
959	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
960	        parsed = self._validate_trust_input(payload, require_version=False)
961	        if parsed is None:
962	            return 400, {
963	                "error": "source must be a non-empty string, public_key 64 "
964	                "lowercase hex characters and expires_at an integer"
965	            }
966	        source, public_key, expires_at = parsed
967	        with self.store.lock:
968	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
969	            if existing is not None:
970	                if (
971	                    existing["public_key"] == public_key
972	                    and existing["expires_at"] == expires_at
973	                ):
974	                    # Idempotent re-registration: the stored record is reported
975	                    # unchanged, with no new version and no new audit event.
976	                    return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)
977	                return 409, {"error": "trust source already exists with different content"}
978	            record = {
979	                "public_key": public_key,
980	                "expires_at": expires_at,
981	                "version": 1,
982	                "status": TRUST_ACTIVE,
983	            }
984	            self.store.trust_sources[source] = record
985	            self.store.append_audit_event(
986	                EVENT_SOURCE_REGISTERED,
987	                {
988	                    "source": source,
989	                    "public_key": public_key,
990	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
991	                    "version": 1,
992	                },
993	            )
994	            try:
995	                self.store.save()
996	            except BaseException:
997	                # Undo both the registry change and its event together.
998	                self.store.trust_sources.pop(source, None)
999	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
1000	                raise
1001	            return 201, self._trust_record(source, record)

1003	    def rotate_trust_source(self, source: object, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1004	        """POST /v1/trust/sources/{source}/rotate — install a new public key.
1005	
1006	        Requires ``public_key``, ``expires_at`` and ``expected_version``. An
1007	        unknown or already-revoked source returns 404; a stale
1008	        ``expected_version`` returns 409. A successful rotation increments the
1009	        version, keeps the source active and persists the change with an audit
1010	        event atomically.
1011	        """
1012	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1013	            return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1014	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1015	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
1016	        for field in ("public_key", "expires_at", "expected_version"):
1017	            if field not in payload:
1018	                return 400, {"error": f"missing field: {field}"}
1019	        body = dict(payload)
1020	        body["source"] = source
1021	        parsed = self._validate_trust_input(body, require_version=True)
1022	        if parsed is None:
1023	            return 400, {
1024	                "error": "public_key must be 64 lowercase hex characters and "
1025	                "expires_at/expected_version integers"
1026	            }
1027	        _, public_key, expires_at, expected_version = parsed
1028	        with self.store.lock:
1029	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
1030	            if existing is None or existing["status"] == TRUST_REVOKED:
1031	                return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1032	            if existing["version"] != expected_version:
1033	                return 409, {"error": "expected_version does not match the current version"}
1034	            old_record = dict(existing)
1035	            existing["public_key"] = public_key
1036	            existing["expires_at"] = expires_at
1037	            existing["version"] = old_record["version"] + 1
1038	            self.store.append_audit_event(
1039	                EVENT_SOURCE_ROTATED,
1040	                {
1041	                    "source": source,
1042	                    "public_key": public_key,
1043	                    "expires_at": expires_at,
1044	                    "version": existing["version"],
1045	                },
1046	            )
1047	            try:
1048	                self.store.save()
1049	            except BaseException:
1050	                self.store.trust_sources[source] = old_record
1051	                self.store.audit_events.pop()
1052	                raise
1053	            return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)

1055	    def revoke_trust_source(self, source: object, payload: object) -> tuple[int, dict]:
1056	        """POST /v1/trust/sources/{source}/revoke — revoke a trusted source.
1057	
1058	        Requires ``expected_version``. An unknown source returns 404 and a
1059	        version mismatch returns 409; revoking an already-revoked source at the
1060	        recorded version is idempotent (200). A new revocation marks the source
1061	        revoked and is persisted with its audit event atomically.
1062	        """
1063	        if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
1064	            return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1065	        if not isinstance(payload, dict):
1066	            return 400, {"error": "request body must be a JSON object"}
1067	        if "expected_version" not in payload:
1068	            return 400, {"error": "missing field: expected_version"}
1069	        expected_version = payload["expected_version"]
1070	        if (
1071	            isinstance(expected_version, bool)
1072	            or not isinstance(expected_version, int)
1073	            or expected_version < 1
1074	        ):
1075	            return 400, {"error": "expected_version must be a positive integer"}
1076	        with self.store.lock:
1077	            existing = self.store.trust_sources.get(source)
1078	            if existing is None:
1079	                return 404, {"error": "unknown trust source"}
1080	            if existing["version"] != expected_version:
1081	                return 409, {"error": "expected_version does not match the current version"}
1082	            if existing["status"] == TRUST_REVOKED:
1083	                # Idempotent repeat revocation: no second event, no new write.
1084	                return 200, self._trust_record(source, existing)
1085	            old_status = existing["status"]
1086	            existing["status"] = TRUST_REVOKED
1087	            self.store.append_audit_event(
1088	                EVENT_SOURCE_REVOKED,
1089	                {

1	"""Persistent storage: blockchain, pending set and derived indexes (JSON).
2	
3	The whole state is one JSON document written atomically: a uniquely named
4	``.ledger-*`` snapshot is fsynced in the same directory and then promoted over
5	the main file with ``os.replace`` (followed by a directory fsync). Every
6	successful write advances a monotonic ``generation`` recorded in the
7	snapshot. A crash can therefore only leave behind (a) the previous main file
8	or (b) a fully fsynced snapshot that never got renamed — never a torn file.
9	
10	On startup the main file and every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
11	as recovery candidates. When no file exists at all, the unique genesis block
12	is created; otherwise each candidate is strictly validated (JSON, generation,
13	consecutive heights, prev_hash linkage, recomputed block hashes and Merkle
14	roots, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signature, pending-only-at-tip and
15	mempool/chain de-duplication). The valid snapshot with the highest generation
16	wins and is promoted if it is still a temp file; same-generation content
17	conflicts, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise StateRecoveryError
18	with the offending path and reason — a fresh chain is never silently created.
19	
20	One atomic write persists everything: the chain (each block carries its
21	confirm/rollback ``status``), a small ``state`` summary, the mempool
22	(``pending``), candidate fork chains (``forks``, each a full block list
23	anchored at the canonical genesis and keyed by its tip hash), the
24	confirmed-transaction ``index`` and the confirmed ``accounts`` activity.
25	Derived data (index/accounts) is *rebuilt* from the chain on every load and
26	every save — pending blocks are excluded, so a restart never resurrects
27	unconfirmed transactions into balances. Persisted fork candidates are
28	re-validated on startup and invalid ones are dropped, while canonical-chain
29	invalidity remains fatal. A re-entrant lock serializes all updates, and a
30	class-wide recovery lock serializes startup scans against in-flight writes.
31	"""
32	from __future__ import annotations
33	
34	import json
35	import os
36	import tempfile
37	import threading
38	import time
39	
40	from .models import (
41	    STATUS_CONFIRMED,
42	    STATUS_PENDING,
43	    Block,
44	    Transaction,
45	    compute_block_hash,
46	)
47	from . import crypto

49	# Previous hash of the genesis block.
50	GENESIS_PREV_HASH = "0" * 64
51	
52	# On-disk schema version, stored under "state" so future migrations are possible.
53	STATE_VERSION = 6
54	
55	# Trust lifecycle states for persisted sources.
56	TRUST_ACTIVE = "active"
57	TRUST_REVOKED = "revoked"

59	# Prefix of durable snapshot temp files ("<state>.ledger-<...>") living next to
60	# the main state file. They double as crash-recovery candidates on startup.
61	SNAPSHOT_PREFIX = ".ledger-"

64	class StateRecoveryError(ValueError):
65	    """Raised when no usable on-disk state can be recovered on startup.
66	
67	    Carries the candidate ``path`` that failed and a human-readable ``reason``
68	    so callers can report (or catch) the failure explicitly. The exception is a
69	    ``ValueError`` subclass, so older callers expecting ``ValueError`` on a
70	    corrupt state file keep working.
71	    """
72	
73	    def __init__(self, path: str, reason: str) -> None:
74	        self.path = path
75	        self.reason = reason
76	        super().__init__(f"cannot recover ledger state from {path}: {reason}")

79	class LedgerStore:
80	    def __init__(self, path: str, initial_balance: int | None = None) -> None:
81	        self.path = path
82	        self.chain: list[Block] = []
83	        self.pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
84	        # Candidate fork chains keyed by tip block hash. Each value is the
85	        # fork's full block list (including the shared genesis block).
86	        self.forks: dict[str, list[Block]] = {}

88	        # record stores delivery metadata plus the tip hash of the synced
89	        # candidate chain (kept in ``forks``) and a content fingerprint used
90	        # for same-key retry/idempotency checks.
91	        self.syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}

94	        self.trust_sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
95	        # Keyless trust allowlist {source: expires_at}; preserved verbatim and
96	        # surfaced by GET /v1/trust for offline light clients.
97	        self.allowlist: dict[str, int] = {}
98	        # Append-only audit events, each {"event_id", "kind", "at", ...payload}.
99	        # event_id is the 1-based position in this list.
100	        self.audit_events: list[dict] = []
101	        # Per-identity endowment used for candidate replay checks; recorded in
102	        # the snapshot so recovery validates against the same convention.
103	        self.initial_balance: int | None = initial_balance
104	        # Monotonic counter bumped on every successful atomic write. It is
105	        # persisted with each snapshot and lets startup pick the newest one.
106	        self.generation: int = 0

108	        self.tx_index: dict[str, int] = {}
109	        self.accounts: dict[str, dict] = {}

113	    @property
114	    def lock(self) -> threading.RLock:
115	        return self._lock

117	    # Serializes startup scans/promotions between threads (or two store
118	    # instances on the same path) within one process. All later mutations take
119	    # the per-store re-entrant lock.

122	    def load(self) -> None:
123	        """Recover state from disk on startup.
124	
125	        The main file *and* every sibling ``.ledger-*`` snapshot are treated
126	        as recovery candidates. When none exist at all, the unique genesis
127	        block is created (the established first-start convention); otherwise
128	        every candidate is strictly validated and the valid snapshot with the
129	        highest generation wins. A winning temp snapshot is atomically
130	        promoted over the main file and every judged-older or residual
131	        candidate is removed. Same-generation snapshots with conflicting
132	        content, or a directory with no valid candidate, raise
133	        StateRecoveryError — a fresh chain is never silently created.
134	        """
135	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(self.path)) or "."
136	        with self._recovery_lock:
137	            candidates = self._discover_candidates(directory)
138	            if not candidates:

152	            valid: list[tuple] = []
153	            errors: list[StateRecoveryError] = []
154	            for candidate in candidates:

156	                    data = self._read_candidate(candidate)
157	                    parsed = self._parse_snapshot(candidate, data)
158	                except StateRecoveryError as exc:

161	                valid.append(
162	                    (
163	                        parsed[2],
164	                        candidate,
165	                        parsed[0],
166	                        parsed[1],
167	                        parsed[3],
168	                        parsed[4],
169	                        parsed[5],
170	                        parsed[6],
171	                        parsed[7],
172	                        parsed[8],
173	                    )
174	                )

176	            if not valid:
177	                details = "; ".join(f"{exc.path} ({exc.reason})" for exc in errors)
178	                raise StateRecoveryError(
179	                    directory, f"no valid snapshot candidate found: {details}"
180	                )
181	
182	            max_generation = max(item[0] for item in valid)
183	            top = [item for item in valid if item[0] == max_generation]
184	            reference = self._canonical_view(
185	                top[0][2],
186	                top[0][3],
187	                top[0][4],
188	                top[0][6],
189	                top[0][7],
190	                top[0][8],
191	                top[0][9],
192	            )
193	            for item in top[1:]:

195	                    self._canonical_view(

197	                        item[3],
198	                        item[4],
199	                        item[6],
200	                        item[7],
201	                        item[8],
202	                        item[9],
203	                    )

209	                        f"conflicting snapshots at generation {max_generation}: {paths}",
210	                    )
211	
212	            # Identical same-generation snapshots: keep the main file when it
213	            # is one of them, avoiding a pointless promotion cycle.
214	            main_abs = os.path.abspath(self.path)
215	            winner = top[0]
216	            for item in top:

220	            (
221	                generation,
222	                winner_path,
223	                chain,
224	                pending,
225	                forks,
226	                winner_init_balance,
227	                syncs,
228	                trust_sources,
229	                allowlist,

238	
239	            self.chain = chain

241	            self.forks = forks
242	            self.syncs = syncs
243	            self.trust_sources = trust_sources
244	            self.allowlist = allowlist
245	            self.audit_events = audit_events

256	    def _discover_candidates(self, directory: str) -> list[str]:
257	        """List the main file and sibling .ledger-* snapshots (if any)."""
258	        candidates: list[str] = []
259	        if os.path.exists(self.path):
260	            candidates.append(self.path)
261	        try:
262	            names = sorted(os.listdir(directory))
263	        except OSError:

266	        for name in names:
267	            if name == main_name or not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX):

274	    @staticmethod
275	    def _canonical_view(
276	        chain: list[Block],
277	        pending: dict[str, Transaction],
278	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
279	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] | None = None,
280	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
281	        allowlist: dict[str, int] | None = None,
282	        audit_events: list[dict] | None = None,
283	    ) -> str:
284	        """Order-independent canonical content hash for conflict detection."""
285	        sync_records = [
286	            {
287	                "source": key[0],
288	                "request_id": key[1],

290	                "expires_at": rec["expires_at"],
291	                "fingerprint": rec["fingerprint"],
292	            }

298	        ]

302	                "pending": [pending[tx_id].to_dict() for tx_id in sorted(pending)],
303	                "forks": [

305	                    for tip in sorted(forks)

307	                "syncs": sync_records,

312	            sort_keys=True,

316	    def _cleanup_candidates(self, directory: str) -> None:
317	        """Remove every residual .ledger-* snapshot next to the main file.
318	
319	        After recovery these are by definition unusable leftovers: older
320	        generations, an identical post-promotion residue, or a partially
321	        written (invalid) file. The promoted/main state is never touched.
322	        """
323	        main_name = os.path.basename(self.path)
324	        for name in list(os.listdir(directory)):
325	            if not name.startswith(SNAPSHOT_PREFIX) or name == main_name:
326	                continue

335	    @staticmethod
336	    def _read_candidate(path: str) -> dict:

353	    def _parse_snapshot(

359	        dict[str, list[Block]],

370	        transaction's tx_id and Ed25519 signature, the pending-only-at-tip
371	        rule, and de-duplication between mempool and chain. Returns the parsed

373	        balance. Raises StateRecoveryError on the first defect, with ``path``

383	        state = data.get("state")

402	        chain: list[Block] = []

441	                        f"tx_id (stored {stored_tx_id!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
442	                    )

445	                        f"duplicate transaction {tx.tx_id} in block "

449	                tx_ids.append(tx.tx_id)
450	            # Blocks store transactions in ascending tx_id order.

459	            )

464	        # Mempool: well-formed, no internal duplicates, never overlapping the
465	        # chain (neither confirmed nor pending-block transactions).
466	        pending: dict[str, Transaction] = {}
467	        pending_raw = data.get("pending", [])

472	                fail("pending entry is not a JSON object")
473	            try:
474	                tx = Transaction.from_dict(tx_raw)
475	            except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError) as exc:
476	                fail(f"pending transaction is malformed: {exc}")
477	            self._validate_transaction(path, tx)
478	            if tx_raw.get("tx_id") != tx.tx_id:
479	                fail(
480	                    f"pending transaction has a mismatched tx_id (stored "
481	                    f"{tx_raw.get('tx_id')!r}, recomputed {tx.tx_id})"
482	                )
483	            if tx.tx_id in pending:
484	                fail(f"duplicate pending transaction {tx.tx_id} in mempool")
485	            if tx.tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
486	                fail(
487	                    f"pending transaction {tx.tx_id} already exists in a block"
488	                )
489	            pending[tx.tx_id] = tx
490	
491	        # Cross-check the persisted tip summary against the chain tail.
492	        tip = chain[-1]
493	        if state.get("height") is not None and state["height"] != tip.height:
494	            fail("state.height does not match the chain tip")
495	        if state.get("tip_hash") is not None and state["tip_hash"] != tip.block_hash:
496	            fail("state.tip_hash does not match the chain tip")
497	        if (
498	            state.get("tip_status") is not None
499	            and state["tip_status"] != tip.status
500	        ):
501	            fail("state.tip_status does not match the chain tip")
502	
503	        forks = self._parse_persisted_forks(data.get("forks", []), chain)
504	        # The trust registry is authoritative configuration and must be parsed
505	        # before the sync records, whose sources are re-authorized against it.
506	        trust_sources = self._parse_persisted_trust_sources(
507	            data.get("trust_sources", []), path
508	        )
509	        syncs, synced_tips = self._parse_persisted_syncs(
510	            data.get("syncs", []), forks, chain, trust_sources
511	        )
512	        # A fork brought in only by a sync record loses its right to exist once
513	        # that record is gone (expired/unauthorized/invalid on restart):
514	        # without this, the independently-persisted fork would resurrect as a
515	        # never-expiring candidate. Direct submissions carry no sync record and
516	        # are untouched.
517	        live_tips = {rec["tip_hash"] for rec in syncs.values()}
518	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in chain}
519	        for tip in synced_tips - live_tips - canonical_hashes:
520	            forks.pop(tip, None)
521	        allowlist = self._parse_persisted_allowlist(data.get("allowlist", {}), path)
522	        audit_events = self._parse_persisted_audit_events(
523	            data.get("audit_events", []), path
524	        )
525	        return (
526	            chain,
527	            pending,
528	            generation,
529	            forks,
530	            initial_balance,
531	            syncs,
532	            trust_sources,
533	            allowlist,
534	            audit_events,
535	        )

537	    @staticmethod
538	    def _parse_persisted_trust_sources(
539	        raw: object, path: str
540	    ) -> dict[str, dict]:
541	        """Strictly parse the persisted source-trust registry.
542	
543	        Unlike candidate forks (re-validated and silently dropped when stale),
544	        the trust registry is authoritative configuration: a malformed entry
545	        is snapshot corruption and fails recovery rather than being dropped.
546	        Each record needs a non-empty source, a 64-char lowercase hex public
547	        key, an integer expiry, a positive integer version and a known status.
548	        """
549	        if raw is None:
550	            return {}
551	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
552	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'trust_sources' must be a list")
553	        sources: dict[str, dict] = {}
554	        for entry in raw:
555	            if not isinstance(entry, dict):
556	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source entry must be an object")
557	            source = entry.get("source")
558	            public_key = entry.get("public_key")
559	            expires_at = entry.get("expires_at")
560	            version = entry.get("version")
561	            status = entry.get("status")
562	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
563	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "trust source must be a non-empty string")
564	            if not crypto.is_hex64(public_key):
565	                raise StateRecoveryError(
566	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has an invalid public_key"
567	                )
568	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
569	                raise StateRecoveryError(
570	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
571	                )
572	            if (
573	                isinstance(version, bool)
574	                or not isinstance(version, int)
575	                or version < 1
576	            ):
577	                raise StateRecoveryError(
578	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} version must be a positive integer"
579	                )
580	            if status not in (TRUST_ACTIVE, TRUST_REVOKED):
581	                raise StateRecoveryError(
582	                    path, f"trust source {source!r} has invalid status {status!r}"
583	                )
584	            if source in sources:
585	                raise StateRecoveryError(
586	                    path, f"duplicate trust source {source!r} in snapshot"
587	                )
588	            sources[source] = {
589	                "public_key": public_key,
590	                "expires_at": expires_at,
591	                "version": version,
592	                "status": status,
593	            }
594	        return sources

596	    @staticmethod
597	    def _parse_persisted_allowlist(raw: object, path: str) -> dict[str, int]:
598	        """Strictly parse the keyless ``{source: expires_at}`` allowlist."""
599	        if raw is None:
600	            return {}
601	        if not isinstance(raw, dict):
602	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'allowlist' must be a JSON object")
603	        allowlist: dict[str, int] = {}
604	        for source, expires_at in raw.items():
605	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
606	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, "allowlist source must be a non-empty string")
607	            if isinstance(expires_at, bool) or not isinstance(expires_at, int):
608	                raise StateRecoveryError(
609	                    path, f"allowlist entry {source!r} expires_at must be an integer"
610	                )
611	            allowlist[source] = expires_at
612	        return allowlist

614	    @staticmethod
615	    def _parse_persisted_audit_events(raw: object, path: str) -> list[dict]:
616	        """Strictly parse the append-only audit event log.
617	
618	        Every event is a JSON object carrying an integer ``at`` timestamp and a
619	        string ``kind``; ``event_id`` values must be exactly 1..N with no gaps
620	        or duplicates, since the id is the event's permanent audit position.
621	        Payload fields beyond those three are retained verbatim.
622	        """
623	        if raw is None:
624	            return []
625	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
626	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "'audit_events' must be a list")
627	        events: list[dict] = []
628	        for i, event in enumerate(raw):
629	            if not isinstance(event, dict):
630	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {i + 1} must be an object")
631	            event_id = event.get("event_id")
632	            kind = event.get("kind")
633	            at = event.get("at")
634	            if (
635	                isinstance(event_id, bool)
636	                or not isinstance(event_id, int)
637	                or event_id != i + 1
638	            ):
639	                raise StateRecoveryError(
640	                    path,
641	                    f"audit event at position {i} has event_id {event_id!r}, "
642	                    f"expected {i + 1}",
643	                )
644	            if not isinstance(kind, str) or not kind:
645	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {event_id} needs a kind")
646	            if isinstance(at, bool) or not isinstance(at, (int, float)):
647	                raise StateRecoveryError(path, f"audit event {event_id} needs a numeric 'at'")
648	            events.append(dict(event))
649	        return events

651	    def _parse_persisted_syncs(
652	        self,
653	        syncs_raw: object,
654	        forks: dict[str, list[Block]],
655	        canonical_chain: list[Block],
656	        trust_sources: dict[str, dict] | None = None,
657	    ) -> tuple[dict[tuple[str, str], dict], set[str]]:
658	        """Parse persisted sync records, dropping unusable ones on restart.
659	
660	        A record is kept only when it is structurally valid, has not yet
661	        expired, its source is still an active, unexpired entry of the
662	        persistent trust registry, and its tip references either a surviving
663	        candidate fork or a block on the canonical chain (a synced candidate
664	        may have been adopted). Records whose source is unknown, revoked or
665	        registry-expired, and records pointing at neither surviving location,
666	        are stale orphans and are pruned; invalid records are silently dropped
667	        rather than failing recovery of the canonical chain. The historical
668	        sync_received/sync_adopted/sync_expired audit events are never touched
669	        by this pruning. Also returns the set of every tip any sync record
670	        claims provenance for (including dropped ones), so the caller can drop
671	        forks that only a pruned sync kept alive.
672	        """
673	        if not isinstance(syncs_raw, list):
674	            return {}, set()
675	        now = time.time()
676	        trust_sources = trust_sources or {}
677	        canonical_hashes = {block.block_hash for block in canonical_chain}
678	        syncs: dict[tuple[str, str], dict] = {}
679	        synced_tips: set[str] = set()
680	        for rec_raw in syncs_raw:
681	            if not isinstance(rec_raw, dict):
682	                continue
683	            source = rec_raw.get("source")
684	            request_id = rec_raw.get("request_id")
685	            tip_hash = rec_raw.get("tip_hash")
686	            expires_at = rec_raw.get("expires_at")
687	            fingerprint = rec_raw.get("fingerprint")
688	            if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
689	                continue
690	            if not isinstance(request_id, str) or not request_id:
691	                continue
692	            if not crypto.is_hex64(tip_hash):
693	                continue
694	            # Provenance is recorded even for dropped records: it proves the
695	            # matching fork must not outlive the sync that delivered it.
696	            synced_tips.add(tip_hash)
697	            if (
698	                isinstance(expires_at, bool)
699	                or not isinstance(expires_at, int)
700	                or expires_at <= now
701	            ):
702	                continue
703	            if not isinstance(fingerprint, str) or not fingerprint:
704	                continue
705	            # Re-authorization on restart: the trust decision recorded at
706	            # delivery is re-checked against the current registry. A source
707	            # rotated away, revoked or expired since then invalidates its
708	            # pending records; historical audit events stay queryable.
709	            trusted = trust_sources.get(source)
710	            if (
711	                trusted is None
712	                or trusted.get("status") != TRUST_ACTIVE
713	                or not isinstance(trusted.get("expires_at"), int)
714	                or isinstance(trusted.get("expires_at"), bool)
715	                or trusted["expires_at"] <= now
716	            ):
717	                continue
718	            if tip_hash not in forks and tip_hash not in canonical_hashes:
719	                continue
720	            key = (source, request_id)
721	            if key in syncs:
722	                continue
723	            syncs[key] = {
724	                "tip_hash": tip_hash,
725	                "expires_at": expires_at,
726	                "fingerprint": fingerprint,
727	            }
728	        return syncs, synced_tips

730	    @staticmethod
731	    def _validate_transaction(path: str, tx: Transaction) -> None:
732	        """Recompute a transaction's id and check its Ed25519 signature."""
733	        if (
734	            not isinstance(tx.sender, str)
735	            or not isinstance(tx.recipient, str)
736	            or not tx.sender
737	            or not tx.recipient
738	        ):
739	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "transaction has invalid from/to fields")
740	        if (
741	            isinstance(tx.amount, bool)
742	            or not isinstance(tx.amount, int)
743	            or tx.amount <= 0
744	        ):
745	            raise StateRecoveryError(
746	                path, f"transaction {getattr(tx, 'sender', '?')} has non-positive amount"
747	            )
748	        if not isinstance(tx.signature, str) or not tx.signature:
749	            raise StateRecoveryError(path, "transaction is missing a signature")
750	        if not crypto.verify_signature(tx.sender, tx.message, tx.signature):
751	            raise StateRecoveryError(
752	                path, f"transaction {tx.tx_id} has an invalid signature"
753	            )

765	    def rebuild_derived(self) -> None:
766	        """Rebuild the confirmed-only transaction index and account activity.
767	
768	        Pending blocks are excluded: only confirmed blocks contribute to
769	        balances and to the tx_id -> height index.
770	        """
771	        self.tx_index = {}
772	        self.accounts = {}
773	        for block in self.chain:
774	            if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
775	                continue
776	            for tx in block.transactions:
777	                self.tx_index[tx.tx_id] = block.height
778	                for account in (tx.sender, tx.recipient):
779	                    entry = self.accounts.setdefault(
780	                        account, {"sent": 0, "received": 0, "transactions": []}
781	                    )
782	                    entry["transactions"].append(tx.tx_id)
783	                self.accounts[tx.sender]["sent"] += tx.amount
784	                self.accounts[tx.recipient]["received"] += tx.amount
